_comment: Expected outputs are generated by the oracle, but the ORACLE'S ORDER is only one valid answer.
Where a problem does not specify an order, exact comparison would reject correct code, so the
exact             the default; results must match element for element
unordered         top-level order is free (each element itself is ordered)
unordered-nested  neither the outer list nor the inner lists have a specified order
Add to this file whenever a correct solution is wrongly rejected; that is a test-data bug.
_skip_comment: LeetCode marks a problem `manual: true` when its own harness serialises the input or output
specially, and for these the published metaData does not describe the real signature (clone-graph
claims integer[][] -> boolean). Generating from it would produce confidently wrong expectations,
so they are skipped until each gets a purpose-built codec.

skip.clone-graph: metaData is manual and misdescribes the signature; needs a Node graph codec
skip.encode-and-decode-strings: entry point is a dummy; needs an encode/decode round-trip harness
skip.copy-list-with-random-pointer: needs a codec for the random pointer
skip.linked-list-cycle: input builds a cycle from pos; needs a cyclic list codec
skip.lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-searc: p and q are node values that must resolve to nodes
